expectations.text: A: Identifies that `innerHTML` does NOT process `<template shadowrootmode>` (the DSD spec)
expectations.evidence: Step 2: 'when you write `wrapper.innerHTML = renderToString(...)`, the `<template shadowrootmode="open">…</template>` stays as a literal `<template>` child of your custom element. It is not unwrapped. The element has no shadow root.' Also explicitly named in step 1: fragment parsers including `innerHTML` do not process DSD.

expectations.text: B: Recommends `setHTMLUnsafe` (or `Document.parseHTMLUnsafe`) as the correct API
expectations.evidence: The Fix section: 'Use **`setHTMLUnsafe`** (or `Document.parseHTMLUnsafe` for a document-scoped variant)' with a code example showing `wrapper.setHTMLUnsafe(html)`.

expectations.text: C: Explains the consequence chain: no shadowRoot at parse time → `hasServerContent === false` → `connectedCallback` runs `fullRender` instead of `hydrate`
expectations.evidence: Steps 3-5 lay out the full chain: constructor sees `this.shadowRoot` is null, `_hydrating` stays false; connectedCallback evaluates `hasServerContent = this.shadowRoot && this.shadowRoot.childNodes.length > 0` to false; component falls through to `this.fullRender(prototypeTemplate)` instead of hydrate.

expectations.text: D: Notes that the failure is silent (no error) — the test "succeeds" but is testing a different code path than intended
expectations.evidence: Opening line: 'There is no error — the element is in the page, the `rendered` event fires, but it fired for the wrong reason. You are not testing hydration; you are testing a fresh client render that happens to start from a server-rendered string.' Reinforced in the closing section: 'There is no error and no warning. Tests pass for the wrong reason.'

expectations.text: E: Mentions that the browser's main HTML parser DOES process DSD; the limitation is on fragment parsers (`innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML`)
expectations.evidence: Step 1: 'The browser's **main HTML parser** processes `<template shadowrootmode="open">` natively — that's why an SSR'd page works in production. But the **fragment parsers** (`innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML`) **do not**. The DSD spec deliberately opts those out because injecting attacker-controlled HTML into an existing shadow root is an XSS escalation vector.'
